craft_claim: Readers automatically infer a character's emotional state from described behavior, objects, and situation even when no emotion word appears; a mismatching emotion word slows comprehension.

supporting_evidence.note: Across priming and reading-time experiments, readers represented characters' emotional states; emotion words that mismatched the implied state produced slower responding, indicating the expected emotion was already represented.
Foregrounded textual features reliably evoked feeling in readers, supporting the view that selected surface detail, not stated emotion, drives affective response.

counterevidence.note: Inference still depends on some emotional involvement; if the surrounding narrative has produced no transportation, the inferred emotion may not be felt.

scope: Narrative comprehension across fiction and narrative nonfiction.
exceptions: Technical exposition or pure dialogue in which no situation model of a character is established.
